clue.text: Stubborn duke, say, a much admired figure after return

indicators.note: after return says the whole run of pieces is then read backwards

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated eg
an idolised person is called a god

explanation.surface: A stubborn aristocrat returns to a hero's welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after return' turns the whole run D + EG + GOD backwards. 'Duke, say' looks like an example being offered; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tenacious who refuses to give up is described as persistent and unyielding.

clue.text: College official largely hated scruffy tie

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a dean is a senior college official

indicators.note: scruffy suggests messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A college administrator loathes a messy necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the N from DEAN, and 'scruffy' rearranges HATED into DHEAT. The definition is a tie in a race, not a necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: A race finishing level, with no winner, is a draw.

clue.text: Poet captures time with universal appeal showing gift

indicators.note: captures says one piece holds the others inside

parts.note: Thomas Gray was the English poet of the Elegy in a Country Churchyard
U is the British film certificate meaning universal
it means sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A poet's charming work proves a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captures' puts T, U and IT inside GRAY. U is the British film rating for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a present of money for service.

clue.text: College celebrity promoted

indicators.note: promoted, raised up, reads the word upwards in a down light

parts.note: note means fame or distinction, as in 'a person of note'

explanation.surface: A famous figure is given a college place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' reads NOTE upward. Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is a renowned English school, formally Eton College.

clue.text: Item for feet and legs, maybe, not black, put into question

indicators.note: put into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to poll people is to question them in a survey

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for black

parts.note: legs are an example of limbs
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Something to do with feet and legs is quizzed, with black excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes B (black) from LIMBS to leave LIMS, which 'put into' places inside POLL. A plimsoll is a British word for a canvas gym shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A plimsoll is a light canvas sports shoe, footwear worn in school PE lessons.

clue.text: What prevents strikes eaus ing property damage?

definitions.text: What prevents strikes eaus ing property damage

parts.words: What prevents strikes eaus ing property damage
parts.note: looks like an industrial-relations measure stopping walkouts; really a metal rod deflecting bolts from the sky

explanation.surface: A way of averting industrial action that harms premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal conductor on a roof carries electrical discharge safely to earth.

clue.text: Written record disregarding Irish office document

indicators.note: disregarding says the following letters are ignored and dropped

parts.note: a memoir is a written account of experiences

explanation.surface: A written account ignores an Irish office paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarding' removes IR from MEMOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A short internal note circulated in a workplace.

clue.text: Decorated part of Cretan robe taken up

indicators.note: taken up says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters are found inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fancy portion of a Cretan robe is shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Decorated part' as the definition, but 'part of' is the hidden-word indicator. 'taken up' reads ETANRO upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborately ornamented is fancy and embellished.

clue.text: Hate group around acting man

indicators.note: around says one piece goes about the other

parts.note: a lot is a group or set, as at an auction
A is short for acting, as in a job title
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A group surrounds an actor and detests him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts LOT about A; then HE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to feel intense dislike.

clue.text: A short set of intricate windings just after river

indicators.note: short tells us to cut the final letter of the word

parts.note: a maze is a network of winding paths
on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: A labyrinth is found close by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last E from MAZE to give MAZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is the great South American river, the largest in the world by volume.

clue.text: An aim eg distorted in which oneself's first to appear?

definitions.text: An aim eg distorted in which oneself's first to appear?

indicators.note: in which says the next piece goes inside the rearranged letters
distorted says the letters of these words are rearranged
first picks out the opening letter of the word oneself's

explanation.surface: A vain person's goal is that they come first in everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges AN AIM EG, and 'in which' puts O, the first letter of 'oneself's', inside. The whole clue also describes the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive self-centredness puts one's own ego ahead of all others.

clue.text: Rather mean English depressed the northern youth left inside large company

annotationWithheld.why: Rather mean English depressed the northern youth left inside large company: BELOW THE BELT; no parse found for the letters BE from 'northern youth'
annotationWithheld.clue: Rather mean English depressed the northern youth left inside large company

clue.text: Catch one deposited in port after docking

indicators.note: deposited in says one piece is placed inside another
docking means cutting off the tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Hull is an English port city on the Humber
A means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: A ship's catch is unloaded at a harbour once moored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after docking' cuts the last L from HULL to give HUL, and 'deposited in' places A inside it. Hull is a port in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A haul is the quantity of fish taken in one netting.

clue.text: Insignificant type poorly keeping time

indicators.note: keeping says one piece holds another inside
poorly suggests the word is in bad shape and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A badly made font letter keeps time in a trivial way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges TYPE into PETY, and 'keeping' holds T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is of little importance or consequence.

clue.text: University volunteers beginning to hate state

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of the word hate

explanation.surface: Student volunteers start to resent a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British army's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, in the Mountain West.

clue.text: Smell associated with your old Highland cottage

parts.note: BO is body odour, an unpleasant smell
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Your ancient Scottish cottage has a smell about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a Scottish hut used by walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bothy is a basic hut or shelter in the Scottish hills.

clue.text: Country in which governor is inspired by start of year?

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Jan, January, is the first month of the year
governor, guv'nor, is old slang for father, so Pa

explanation.surface: A country whose ruler draws inspiration from New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is inspired by' puts PA inside JAN. 'Governor' is British slang for father or boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is an island nation in East Asia.

clue.text: Very large car in MOT also requiring restoration

indicators.note: restoration suggests these letters must be rebuilt into new order

explanation.surface: An old car that has failed its MOT test needs restoring.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars. 'requiring restoration' rearranges CAR IN MOT ALSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical figures are enormous, like the distances between stars.

clue.text: Who's designed tender, maybe, gets to behave ostentatiously

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are arranged into a new form

parts.note: a tender is a small boat serving a ship

explanation.surface: Someone asks who designed a small vessel, a chance to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges WHOS into SHOW. A tender is a boat, not a soft feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To show off is to flaunt oneself and seek attention.

clue.text: Cap endlessly worn by single dark female

indicators.note: worn by says one piece is wrapped around the other
endlessly says the last letter goes

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo
a single in cricket is one run

explanation.surface: A hat with no end worn by a lone dark-haired woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' is a verb, to outdo. 'endlessly' trims BETTER to BETTE and 'worn by' puts RUN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark brown hair.

clue.text: One required to make snap judgments?

definitions.text: One required to make snap judgments?

parts.words: One required to make snap judgments?
parts.note: looks like a hasty decision-maker; really someone whose job is choosing when to take snaps, or pictures

explanation.surface: A person forced into hasty decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera operator decides the instant to take each snapshot.

clue.text: Tremble at source of missiles

definitions.meaning: a case holding arrows that an archer draws from

explanation.definitionFit: Both a slight shaking and an archer's arrow case.

clue.text: Retreat set up beside Venetian district

indicators.note: set up reads the word upwards in a down light

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den or retreat
to can mean close against, as in 'cheek to cheek'

explanation.surface: A hideaway is raised next to a part of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reads LAIR upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the commercial area of Venice around its famous bridge.

clue.text: Fellow removed from inappropriate section of army

indicators.note: removed from says a letter is taken out of the following word

parts.note: unfit means unsuitable or inappropriate

explanation.surface: A colleague is dismissed from an unsuitable army post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes F out of UNFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit is a detachment or formation of soldiers.

clue.text: One in siege, leading figure and knight

parts.note: the hero is the main character in a story
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A soldier in a besieged town, a champion and a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'siege' is the collective noun for a group of these birds, so 'siege' misleads you toward warfare.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of these wading birds is traditionally called a siege.

clue.text: American writer lacking a counterpart

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word

parts.note: Mark Twain was the American author of Huckleberry Finn

explanation.surface: An American novelist has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes A from TWAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching pair of things or people are exact duplicates of each other.

clue.text: Husband at one time gets fine weapon

definitions.note: husband here is an old verb, to cultivate land

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A former spouse gets a good weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' is an archaic verb meaning to manage or till land, not a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To till and cultivate land is the old meaning of husbanding it.

clue.text: Accommodating learner, get rid of mechanism in car

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to axe is to get rid of
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: Housing a learner driver, someone ditches part of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodating' puts L inside AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod on which car wheels turn.

clue.text: Country resident recalling bitterness in struggle by river

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

indicators.note: recalling, calling back, says the word is read backwards

parts.note: gall means bitterness or rancour

explanation.surface: A rural dweller remembers resentment from a fight by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' turns GALL into LLAG, and 'in' puts it inside VIE, then R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in a small rural settlement rather than a town.

clue.text: Specialist with love for energy commodity

indicators.note: with ... for says one letter replaces another in the word

parts.note: an expert is a specialist
E is the physics symbol for energy
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: An expert puts love before energy in trading goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with love for energy' swaps an E in EXPERT for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold abroad are traded overseas as products.

clue.text: One sharing quarters returning secure before end of game

indicators.note: returning says the word comes back the other way

parts.note: to moor a boat is to secure it
mate, checkmate, ends a game of chess

explanation.surface: A flatmate comes back to lock up before a match finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns MOOR into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who lives in the same room or flat as another.

clue.text: Principally, kitchen equipment that tea lovers employ

definitions.text: Principally, kitchen equipment that tea lovers employ

indicators.note: principally takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: An item every tea drinker uses in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principally' takes the first letters of the six words after it, and the whole clue also describes the item.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiling appliance is what tea drinkers use to heat water.
